Vulnerability Analysis

🔴 Critical Vulnerabilities

1. Sensitive Information Disclosure (PII)

CVSS 9.1 CWE-359 WASC-13

Technical Description:
  • Personal user information is publicly accessible without authentication
  • Direct violation of data confidentiality principles
  • Clear breach of GDPR requirements
Business Impact:

  • Reputation Damage: Significant loss of customer trust

🟠 High Priority Vulnerabilities

2. Missing Subresource Integrity (SRI)

CVSS 6.2 | 5 instances

Description: External resources loaded without integrity verification, creating supply chain attack risks.

3. Absent Content Security Policy (CSP)

CVSS 5.8 | 5 instances

Description: Missing content security policy exposes site to XSS and injection attacks.

4. Missing Clickjacking Protection

CVSS 5.5 | 5 instances

Description: Absence of X-Frame-Options headers enables iframe-based clickjacking attacks.

OWASP Top 10 2021 Compliance Analysis

❌ A01:2021 – Broken Access Control

Status: CRITICAL FAILURE

PII disclosure directly violates access control principles. Sensitive information protection mechanisms are absent.

❌ A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration

Status: CRITICAL FAILURE

Missing security headers (CSP, HSTS), no clickjacking protection, improper configuration across multiple vectors.

⚠️ A03:2021 – Injection

Status: COMPLIANT

No SQL injection, NoSQL injection, or OS command injection vulnerabilities detected.

Remediation Plan

Phase 1: Critical Fixes (Days 0-7)

Days 1-3: Eliminate PII Disclosure

  • Immediately identify and block PII exposure vectors
  • Implement encryption for sensitive data
  • Notify regulatory authorities per GDPR requirements (72-hour window)

Days 4-7: Implement Basic Security Headers

  • Deploy Content Security Policy
  • Configure X-Frame-Options: DENY
  • Implement HSTS with preload
  • Validate all changes on staging

Phase 2: High Priority Fixes (Weeks 2-4)

  • Implement Subresource Integrity for all external resources
  • Add X-Content-Type-Options header
  • Configure additional security headers
  • Audit and update all WordPress components

Phase 3: Long-term Improvements (Months 2-3)

  • Deploy security monitoring (SIEM)
  • Implement centralized logging
  • Create incident response procedures
  • Establish continuous security training program
